title: Mutually beneficial interactions between bacteria and Arabidopsis promote phosphorus nutrition and growth.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: paper_context.py: no PMCID, Europe PMC flags all N (not open access, no supplement, no data links, no text-mined accessions), no NCBI GEO/SRA/BioProject links, no Zenodo/Dryad hit on the DOI. One web search found only the PubMed and ScienceDirect landing pages, with no data repository named.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Abstract only: root-bacterial isolates tested for helping seedlings take up phosphorus (P), a mechanistic Acinetobacter–malate story, and soil experiments. No sample counts, file formats or accessions were visible.

a1_downloadable.note: No downloadable dataset found: the paper is paywalled with no PMC copy, and there are no repository links (GEO, SRA, Zenodo, Dryad) or accessions anywhere. Checked through the APIs, not the publisher site.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not checkable without files. The plausible label (how much each bacterial isolate boosts plant P or growth) would be a per-isolate table from plate assays, probably only in a paywalled supplement.

a3_inputs_present.note: No isolate genomes or 16S (bacterial marker gene) sequences found deposited, so no inputs were confirmed.

a5_enough_rows.note: Row count unknown. Mechanistic studies of root-microbiome isolate collections usually test tens to a few hundred strains, likely under 400.

a6_fits_laptop.note: An isolate phenotype table would be tiny, if it existed.

a8_label_provenance.note: A growth or P-uptake readout would be a physical measurement, but none was seen.

backbone.name: Possible: a bacterial genome or protein language model (e.g. ESM-2 on isolate proteomes), but untested

integration.partner_dataset: At-RSPHERE/AtSPHERE Arabidopsis root bacterial culture collection genomes (not checked)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do bacterial genome features predict which root isolates help plants take up phosphorus?

controls.positive_control: Known phosphate-solubilising genes (e.g. pqq genes for gluconic-acid production) should predict P mobilisation

honest_claim_h3: At best: predicts which isolates from one Arabidopsis root collection boost seedling P uptake on agar plates in one lab; there is no data to back even this.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use bacterial genome content to predict whether a root bacterium helps Arabidopsis seedlings take up phosphorus.
plain_idea.train_on: One row per bacterial isolate with its genome; the number of isolates is unknown.
plain_idea.predict: Change in seedling phosphorus content or growth when co-cultured with the isolate, measured in the paper's plate assays.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Groups designing microbial products that reduce fertiliser use could screen strain collections by genome before running plant assays.

ml_idea: Predict plant-growth-promoting P phenotype per isolate from genome features; not feasible without a deposited isolate phenotype table.

effort.cheapest_killing_check: Get the Cell supplement and count isolates with a measured P or growth phenotype; under 400 kills it.

verdict_reason: A1 fails: the paper is paywalled, and no deposited data, accessions or supplement could be found through Europe PMC, NCBI, Zenodo or Dryad. It is also a mechanistic study whose isolate count is probably too small (A5) even if a supplement table exists.
